notes: Eclipse Loop 2.4.1 A real audio fix, and three arranger things that should always have been there. Transients are no longer eaten at a stretch boundary If you have used Quantize or Warp, this one is worth updating for. Eclipse's time-stretcher builds its output from overlapping grains. Two of them sum to unity in the middle of a stretch — but the first grain had nothing overlapping its opening half, so every stretched segment began with a short ramp up from silence. That would be a harmless edge artefact if it happened somewhere quiet. It didn't. Audio quantize cuts the audio at the transients, so every hit it moved landed at the very start of its own segment — exactly where the ramp was. A drum hit came out at 0.0019 of its input level: 54 dB down, on the precise thing you were lining up. The same applied to any warp split by a tempo change. Fixed. Transients now survive a stretch at full level. It went unnoticed because the test suite checked that quantized audio was not silent and had no gaps — both true — and never checked its level. There is now a test that puts a click exactly on a stretch boundary and requires it to come through
